column1: # libsais reference vectors for the ESA suffix array / LCP (work package 1a.6, docs/refactoring/suffix-tree-upgrade/PROGRESS-S1.md).
# Oracle: libsais v2.9.1, commit 1aae6344b8a58f00626f001b1fe33bdbecd5e469 (https://github.com/IlyaGrebnov/libsais, pinned in analysis/bench/SOURCES.txt),
#         Release build with gcc 13.3.0 -O3 (static library, OpenMP flag of the handoff build, single-threaded entry points only).
#         Byte texts: libsais + libsais_plcp + libsais_lcp. UTF-16 texts (a code unit above 255 occurs): libsais16 + libsais16_plcp + libsais16_lcp.
#         No libsais code or binary is in this repository; the throw-away C driver lived outside it.
# Definitions (n = text length; "ours" = SaisReference / LcpReference, layout with n + 1 entries):
#   sa_sha256  = SHA-256 of the libsais SA[0..n-1] written as n little-endian int32 = our SA[1..n]  (libsais has no entry for the empty suffix;
#                ours has SA[0] = n, which is skipped). Suffix order is ordinal by code unit, a proper prefix sorts first, in both.
#   lcp_sha256 = SHA-256 of the libsais LCP[0..n-1] (libsais_lcp over libsais_plcp) as n little-endian int32 = our LCP[1..n].
#                libsais: LCP[0] = 0 and LCP[i] = lcp(suffix SA[i-1], suffix SA[i]).  Ours: LCP[1] = 0 (predecessor is the empty suffix) and
#                LCP[r] = lcp(suffix SA[r-1], suffix SA[r]) for r >= 2; hence libsais LCP[i] == our LCP[i + 1].
#   width      = u8: the text has only code units <= 255 (one byte each); u16: raw UTF-16 code units.
#   kind = file       the benchmark input data/<corpus>.txt (bytes of the file, no terminator, no newline), regenerated by analysis/bench/gen/gen_inputs.py
#                     and checked against analysis/bench/MANIFEST.sha256 before use.
#   kind = generated  StringFamilies.Adversarial(n, seed = 1) of tests/SuffixTree/SuffixTree.Esa.Tests/TestSupport, n in {100000, 1000000}, the family name
#                     (parameters and seed included) + "-n<N>" is the corpus name; all-distinct (sigma = n) exists only up to n = 65536 and is listed at n = 65536.
# Checks done by the driver on every corpus when this file was produced: Kasai LCP computed from the libsais SA equals libsais_lcp, the SA is a
# permutation of 0..n-1, and for texts with all units <= 255 the 16-bit entry points give the same SA and LCP hashes as the byte entry points.
# The driver itself was validated against a naive suffix sort and the LCP definition on 40,000 random small texts (both widths).
# Test: tests/SuffixTree/SuffixTree.Esa.Tests/Vectors (category Vectors, [Explicit]; inputs: set SEQERON_BENCH_DIR to a regenerated bench directory).
